question:
Refer to the exhibit. A network engineer must retrieve the network interface name from a JSON object. The engineer loads the JSON into a Python dictionary named json_object. Which code snippet completes the Python script?
import json

json_object = {
  "type": "network",
  "if-name": "eth0",
  "description": "ethernet",
  "ip-address": "170.15.15.11",
  "subnet-mask": "255.255.255.0",
  "nat-direction": ""
}
______
return interface_name
theory: json_object is already a Python dictionary once the JSON text has been parsed, so a value is retrieved using its exact string key from the document — here 'if-name' — with bracket notation: json_object["if-name"]. Indexing with an integer (json_object[0]) or using the value itself as though it were the key ("eth0") doesn't correspond to how dictionaries are addressed in Python. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
